goal: Teach Year-2 physics students to turn a physical random trial into reproducible Monte Carlo evidence, interpret mean and spread, and validate a stochastic simulation.

sample_generation_method.input_context_preparation: parent inspected local strict MATLAB references with view_image; approved sample supplied as style reference
sample_generation_method.handoff_rule: Use the built-in image_gen tool in edit/reference mode only; return a blocker if unavailable.

style.name: Teaching Courseware - PHY4605 approved sample
style.visual_direction: Open white canvas; title-only navy band with a thin straight navy divider below; large bold navy sans-serif title; muted navy structure with restrained teal, sage, and ochre accents; generous spacing; quantitative teaching visuals; no outer border or top mini-header.
style.color_palette: white/light neutral, navy, teal, sage green, muted ochre, occasional coral only for genuine defects
style.typography: large bold sans-serif title, readable regular sans-serif body, short monospaced MATLAB code only when required
style.deck_consistency: Use the approved sample for visual rhythm; vary internal composition by slide role; no slide number, logo, watermark, or decorative perimeter.

approved_style_reference.role: approved Week 10 sample slide style reference
approved_style_reference.fidelity: match title band, divider, palette, typography and density only; never copy its histogram layout unless appropriate

deck_context.source_summary: One trial is a complete 100-step one-dimensional symmetric random walk starting at x=0 mm with independent ±1 mm steps. Repeat M paths, inspect the final-position distribution, interpret centre and spread, validate symmetry and parity, and use rng(4605,'twister') only for reproducibility.
deck_context.locked_values: N=100; a=1 mm; M=100, 1000, 10000; mean final positions 0.040, 0.066, -0.128 mm; population spreads 10.6320, 9.8122, 9.9423 mm; ideal spread a*sqrt(N)=10 mm; standard errors 1.0632, 0.3103, 0.0994 mm.
deck_context.universal_constraints: Use title-only top band and a thin straight divider. Do not render headers, slide numbers, page footers, borders, logos, timings, production metadata, or unapproved numerical claims.

slides.title: Can Random Motion Produce a Stable Pattern?
slides.intent: Open with the physical question before code.
key_points: Many paths may have a centre near zero and nonzero spread

layout.composition: question-led particle sketch with two prediction cards

visual_elements.main_visual: particle receiving equal left/right random kicks

constraints: Use a compact prediction prompt; no data graph.
slides.local_context: A random walk has no preferred direction, but individual histories differ.

slides.title: Define One Random Trial Before Coding
slides.intent: Separate one physical path from repeated trials.
key_points: Start x = 0 mm; step length = 1 mm

layout.composition: nested diagram: one path inside a collection of repeated paths

visual_elements.main_visual: clearly labelled N=100 path versus M repeated paths

slides.local_context: Do not confuse steps per path N with Monte Carlo trial count M.

slides.title: Read the Random-Step Rule in Physics Language
slides.intent: Map each random draw to a physical displacement.
key_points: Each step is +1 mm or -1 mm
Equal probability means no preferred direction
N changes the process; M changes the evidence

layout.composition: two labelled step arrows beside N versus M comparison

slides.title: Plan the Monte Carlo Experiment
slides.intent: Show the computation chain before MATLAB.

layout.composition: five-stage horizontal flow ending in validation

slides.local_context: Algorithm: model, random steps, path, repeated endpoints, statistics and validation.

slides.title: Use a Seed for a Reproducible Random Sequence
slides.intent: Distinguish a computational seed from a model parameter.
key_points: Same seed plus same code repeats results
A different seed can still give a valid result

layout.composition: two matching code-to-output paths contrasted with one different valid path

slides.local_context: Fixed seed helps exact reruns; it does not replace validation.

slides.title: Read the Random-Sampling Scaffold
slides.intent: Trace random draws into physical steps.

layout.composition: large readable strict code block with short arrows to uniform draw, direction, and step

constraints: Preserve code tokens exactly; use readable regular monospaced type.
slides.local_context: Uniform draws below 0.5 become -1; draws at least 0.5 become +1.

slides.title: One Trajectory Is One Possible History
slides.intent: Connect a single path to a stochastic history.
key_points: Another seed gives another valid path
One path cannot determine mean or spread

layout.composition: large cohesive redraw of supplied trajectory with two short callouts

required_images.fidelity: preserve axes Step number and Position x (mm), line path, highlighted markers, values and relationships in a full-slide redraw

slides.local_context: Trajectory begins at 0 mm and ends at 18 mm after 100 steps; do not imply it is typical.

slides.title: Repeat the Trial to Build a Distribution
slides.intent: Use the approved sample to show repeated random evidence.
key_points: The distribution is broad but centred near zero
slides.local_context: Approved sample. Its histogram is a cohesive redraw of the 10,000 endpoint distribution and labels mean -0.128 mm.

slides.title: Mean and Spread Answer Different Questions
key_points: A mean near zero does not mean every particle ends near zero

layout.composition: broad endpoint strip with distinct centre and spread annotations

slides.local_context: Mean is a centre; spread is real physical trial-to-trial variation.

slides.title: More Trials Do Not Remove Physical Variability
slides.intent: Compare evidence quantity with physical spread.

layout.composition: three-row table plus one concise interpretation callout

slides.local_context: More trials stabilise estimates; they do not remove the physical spread of individual endpoints.

slides.title: Monte Carlo Convergence Need Not Be Monotonic
slides.intent: Interpret one finite random sequence honestly.
key_points: The 1000-trial result is farther from zero than the 100-trial result
More trials generally stabilise; one sequence need not approach monotonically

layout.composition: large cohesive redraw of supplied log-scale graph with non-monotonic callout

required_images.fidelity: preserve log-scale trial-count axis, zero line, three points, axes, units and non-monotonic relationship in a full-slide redraw

slides.title: Validate With Symmetry and the Step Rule
key_points: Symmetry predicts a long-run mean near 0 mm
After 100 ±1 mm steps every endpoint is an even integer mm
The locked simulation passes both checks

layout.composition: two equal validation cards: symmetry and parity

visual_elements.main_visual: balance diagram and even-position number line

slides.local_context: A plausible histogram or fixed seed is not itself validation.

slides.title: Working Exposure: Precision and Random-Walk Scaling
slides.intent: Interpret supplied precision and ideal scaling without derivation.
key_points: Ideal spread a*sqrt(N) = 10 mm; simulation gives 9.9423 mm

layout.composition: two light working-exposure panels with a clear Core/Working distinction

constraints: Mark this as Working exposure; no derivation.
slides.local_context: Standard error concerns the estimated mean, not physical spread.

slides.title: Explain One Trial, One Statistic, and One Check
key_points: Choose and explain one validation check

layout.composition: three open response cards on an open canvas

slides.local_context: Also ask why two correct runs can differ and when a fixed seed is useful.
